summary: Unfold [B] for Y (integral_besselMeasure_eq_of_mean), swap the integrals, unfold [B′] for Y′; the means over the unipotent radicals turn the product of the two constant terms into the zero term of the arrow product (the identity hz), and the zero term intertwines the triple Weil action. (Lines 59–63 are the rest of the statement after its `let F g r :=`; the line census reads them as part of the value, so they stand in the introduction.)

steps.claim: Choose z ≠ 0 (h) with θ(f ⊠ f′) = z·θ(f)θ(f′) (M, theta_arrowProduct for V, V′, V″); B: the formula for the form adjoint; κ, K: the Bessel unfolding for Y (integral_besselMeasure_eq_of_mean); and from string_spec: s odd (O), s′ = s − 1, s″ = s′ − 1, c(Y′) = c(Y) (c).
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨⟨z, h, M⟩, B, ⟨κ, K⟩, O, ⟨⟩, ⟨⟩, c⟩ := theta_arrowProduct V V' V'',
    Y.formAdjoint_apply Y', Y.integral_besselMeasure_eq_of_mean (.refl _), D.string_spec

steps.claim: For data f, f′ and points w, w′: constTerm_Y(f, w)·constTerm_{Y′}(f′, w′) = z⁻¹·zeroTerm(homHeisOp(w)f ⊠ homHeisOp(w′)f′)(0), the zero term along homZeroPart(D).
steps.lean:
have hz f f' w w' : Y.constTerm Y'.gradeOf f w * Y'.constTerm Y''.gradeOf f' w' =
    z⁻¹ * D.homZeroPart.splitting.zeroTerm (arrowProduct (homHeisOp w f) (homHeisOp w' f')) 0 := by
    rw [eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq₀ h, Splitting.zeroTerm_apply,
      ← quotMean_quotMean (_root_.ratVectors ..) _ (_root_.ratVectors ..) (.mk' (fun a ↦
      matToVec ((V.formAdjoint V' (vecToMat a.1)).fromRows (vecToMat a.2)) ∘ val) (id _)) _ _
      (val_injective.surjective_comp_right.forall.2 fun b ↦ ⟨(matToVec (V'.formAdjoint V
      (vecToMat b).toRows₁), matToVec (vecToMat b).toRows₂), by simp [-vecToMat]⟩)]
    any_goals rintro _ ⟨a, ⟨⟩⟩ _ ⟨b, ⟨⟩⟩
    any_goals simp [↓isContPeriodic_along_k, continuous_pi_iff, mem_ratVectors, B, ← map_mul,
      ratAdeles, -continuous_prodMk, funext_iff, add_mul, mul_add] <;> constructor <;> fun_prop
    simp_rw [constTerm, quotMean, ← integral_mul_const, ← integral_const_mul, ← θ_ϱ, ← M,
      ← homHeisOp_arrowProduct, homHeisOp, ← x_inv_mulVec_matToVec, mulVec_zero, zero_add]; congr!
    apply (kAdelic_mulVec _ rfl _).symm.trans (congrArg ..) <;> simp +contextual [funext_iff, B]
steps.typed_fact:
Y.constTerm Y'.gradeOf f w * Y'.constTerm Y''.gradeOf f' w' =
    z⁻¹ * D.homZeroPart.splitting.zeroTerm (arrowProduct (homHeisOp w f) (homHeisOp w' f')) 0

steps.claim: Clear z, write the zero term as a mean over rational vectors, and split it into iterated means over the two blocks (quotMean_quotMean along (a, b) ↦ (formAdjoint(a), b), which is onto).
steps.lean:
rw [eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq₀ h, Splitting.zeroTerm_apply,
      ← quotMean_quotMean (_root_.ratVectors ..) _ (_root_.ratVectors ..) (.mk' (fun a ↦
      matToVec ((V.formAdjoint V' (vecToMat a.1)).fromRows (vecToMat a.2)) ∘ val) (id _)) _ _
      (val_injective.surjective_comp_right.forall.2 fun b ↦ ⟨(matToVec (V'.formAdjoint V
      (vecToMat b).toRows₁), matToVec (vecToMat b).toRows₂), by simp [-vecToMat]⟩)]

steps.claim: In the side goals, take the vectors coming from rational points.
steps.lean: any_goals rintro _ ⟨a, ⟨⟩⟩ _ ⟨b, ⟨⟩⟩

steps.claim: The side conditions: continuity and periodicity of the integrands along k, and rationality.
steps.lean:
any_goals simp [↓isContPeriodic_along_k, continuous_pi_iff, mem_ratVectors, B, ← map_mul,
      ratAdeles, -continuous_prodMk, funext_iff, add_mul, mul_add] <;> constructor <;> fun_prop

steps.claim: Unfold constTerm and the means: the product of two means of θ-values is the mean of θ of the arrow product of the translated data (M, homHeisOp_arrowProduct).
steps.lean:
simp_rw [constTerm, quotMean, ← integral_mul_const, ← integral_const_mul, ← θ_ϱ, ← M,
      ← homHeisOp_arrowProduct, homHeisOp, ← x_inv_mulVec_matToVec, mulVec_zero, zero_add]; congr!

steps.claim: The translation vectors agree (kAdelic_mulVec).
steps.lean: apply (kAdelic_mulVec _ rfl _).symm.trans (congrArg ..) <;> simp +contextual [funext_iff, B]

steps.claim: Apply the Bessel unfolding for Y′ along gradeOne of D, with the constant κ·κ′·z⁻¹; introduce its conclusion H, the genericity Q of P and the function F.
steps.lean: refine (Y'.integral_besselMeasure_eq_of_mean D.gradeOne).imp' (κ * · * z⁻¹) ?_; introv H Q F

steps.claim: F is jointly continuous (P is continuous by Q).
steps.lean: have C : Continuous ↿F := Q.rec (by simp [F, *]; fun_prop)

steps.claim: For each r, g ↦ F(g, r) is invariant under the rational points of the Bessel group of Y.
steps.lean:
have L r : Y.ratBessel.FixesLeft (F · r) := fun _ o ↦
    (by simp [F, Q.2 _ o, ← constTermAtT_rat_mul ⟨_, o⟩ 1 ·])

steps.claim: For each g, r ↦ F(g, r) is invariant under the rational points of the Bessel group of Y′.
steps.lean:
have R g : Y'.ratBessel.FixesLeft (F g) := fun δ l r ↦ by
    simp [F, ← constTermAtT_rat_mul 1 ⟨_, l⟩ g r, ← constTermAtT_rat_mul ⟨_, l⟩ 1 r]

steps.claim: For each r, apply K to g ↦ F(g, r): on the unipotent radical F(n·a, r) is a periodic function of the relevant row of n whose mean is the constant term (IsGeneric.unipotent_mul_constTerm, with the degree conditions coming from s odd); so ∫_{[B]} F(·, r) = κ·∫_{[U(X)]} of that mean. Rearrange the constants.
steps.lean:
simp_rw [fun r ↦
    K (L r) C.along_fst (fun n l ↦ by simp [F, mul_assoc n, -mul_assoc, Q.unipotent_mul_constTerm
    Y'.gradeOf_stringReversal l (Y.hasDegreeGe_two_of_odd O l) (Y.hasDegreeGe_neg_one_stringMap.mul
    (Y.hasDegreeGe_two_of_odd O l))]) (fun a ↦ ⟨⟨continuous_const, by simp⟩, quotMean_const
    (F (Y.inclX a) r)⟩) (by fun_prop) (by simp +contextual [L, ↓inclX_mem_ratBessel]), mul_assoc,
    ← integral_const_mul z⁻¹, mul_left_comm (P _), ← integral_const_mul (P _), integral_const_mul κ]

steps.claim: Swap the two integrals (Fubini; the integrand is integrable on the cocompact product).
steps.lean:
rw [integral_integral_swap (integrable_of_cocompact
    (cocompact_prod Y'.isCocompact_ratBessel (stdSpace ..).exists_isCompact_of_definite)
    (by fun_prop) (by simp +contextual [*, ↓inclX_mem_ratBessel]))]; congr with x

steps.claim: Apply H to the function of r: it is invariant (step 6) and continuous; its mean is θ(tripleWeil(a, b)(g, r, embX k)(zeroTerm(…))), because the zero term intertwines the triple Weil actions (zeroTerm_splitting_tripleWeil) and the translation by stackedT commutes with them; the θ-integrand is continuous and rationally invariant (theta_tripleWeil_rat_mul). The value on unipotent elements n remains.
steps.lean:
refine H (R _) C.along_snd (fun n o g ↦ ?_) (fun _ ↦ ⟨isContPeriodic_along_k .., by
    simp_rw [← Splitting.zeroTerm_apply, ← D.zeroTerm_splitting_tripleWeil, stackedT,
      homHeisOp_arrowProduct, ← arrowProduct_twistedPairWeil, pairWeil_homHeisOp,
      inclX_mul_stringMap_mul_inclX_inv, ← homHeisOp_arrowProduct, ← smul_eq_mul, ← map_smul,
      splitting, zeroTerm_comp]; rfl⟩) (by simp [tripleWeil, -circleChar_inv_apply]; fun_prop)
    (one_mul x ▸ by simp +contextual [↓theta_tripleWeil_rat_mul])

steps.claim: Move the Heisenberg translation through the zero term (zeroTerm_rho_iAdelic and the k-part), with Heisenberg cocycle 1 here, and combine the translation vectors (the bicharacter).
steps.lean:
rw [← θ_ϱ, ← zeroTerm_rho_iAdelic, ← zeroTerm_rho_kAdelic
    ((matToVec (stackedT Y Y' Y'' * (V'.ratCoordMatrix n - 1)) - _) ∘ val), (heisRep _).2,
    (by simp [D.homZeroPart.splitting.beta_eq_coords] : Heisenberg.β .. = 1), kAdelic_mulVec _ rfl,
    iAdelic, Space.ratMap, Matrix.mul_assoc, ← mulVec_mulVec, ← mulVec_add, sub_add_cancel,
    x_inv_mulVec_matToVec, (heisRep _).2, ← homBicharacter, homBicharacter_eq, ← Matrix.mul_assoc]

steps.claim: Identify with the product of the two constant terms: the unipotent elements act on them by characters (constTerm_mul for Y and Y′), and stackedT is the form adjoint of the stacked frequency maps:
steps.lean:
· simp [F, one_mul (Y.inclX x) ▸ Y.constTerm_mul Y'.gradeOf_stringReversal (.inr ⟨_,
      Y'.mem_unipotent.1 o⟩) _, one_mul (Y''.inclX k) ▸ Y'.constTerm_mul Y''.gradeOf_stringReversal
      (.inr ⟨o, Y''.mem_unipotent.1 _⟩) _ _, stackedT, ↓show ∀ A B, V'.formAdjoint (flipSum V V'')
      (A.fromRows B) = (-V'.formAdjoint V A).fromCols (V'.formAdjoint V'' B) by simp [formAdjoint,
      flipSpace], formAdjoint_stringMap_mul_stringMap, c, Matrix.mul_sub]
    simp [hz, ← homHeisOp_arrowProduct, formAdjoint_ratCoordMatrix_mul]

steps.claim: The form adjoint of fromRows(A, B) for V⁻ ⊕ V″ is fromCols(−adjoint_V(A), adjoint_{V″}(B)).
steps.lean:
show ∀ A B, V'.formAdjoint (flipSum V V'')
      (A.fromRows B) = (-V'.formAdjoint V A).fromCols (V'.formAdjoint V'' B) by simp [formAdjoint,
      flipSpace]

steps.claim: Adjoints of products of string maps, and c(Y′) = c(Y) (c).
steps.lean: , formAdjoint_stringMap_mul_stringMap, c, Matrix.mul_sub]

steps.claim: Then the identity is the one of step 2.
steps.lean: simp [hz, ← homHeisOp_arrowProduct, formAdjoint_ratCoordMatrix_mul]

steps.claim: The remaining degree condition, for a basis index p of Hom: either p is outside the image of the grade-zero index (h) or it is in it.
steps.lean: intro p r; obtain h | ⟨⟨⟩, ⟨⟩⟩ := not_or_of_imp (D.homZeroPart.mem_range_index p).2

steps.claim: Outside the image, the entry vanishes: incl vanishes there (incl_eq_zero) and stackedT·(ratCoord n − 1) has the required degree (HasDegreeGe.mul with the degrees of the string maps).
steps.lean:
· simp [D.homZeroPart.incl_eq_zero,
      h, ↓HasDegreeGe.mul (w'' := Y.gradeOf ⊕ᵥ Y''.gradeOf) (x := stackedT Y Y' Y'') (Sum.rec (by
      simp +contextual [stackedT, B, Y.hasDegreeGe_neg_one_stringMap _, add_comm])
      Y'.hasDegreeGe_neg_one_stringMap) (Y'.mem_unipotent.1 o) le_rfl p.1 p.2 (by omega)]

steps.claim: In the image, both sides are computed by stackedT_apply of D (entries of stackedT on the zero part are incl times c) and agree.
steps.lean:
simp [homZeroPart, GradeZeroPart.hom, D.stackedT_apply, homTarget, removePlanes, inclMatrix,
    Fintype.sum_prod_type, apply_ite toAdele, Finset.sum_mul,
    Finset.sum_comm, kAdelic, Matrix.mul_assoc]
